tier_reason: Peer-reviewed I3D 2014 paper (copy in the repo) compares against CGAL 4.2 on i7 2600K + GTX 580; compiler/flags only 'compiled with optimization enabled', so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Synthetic distributions: speedup over CGAL starts at 4-6x and rises to 8-10x as input grows; real-world models: 6-9x over CGAL 4.2 (paper, Fig. 6)
corrections.caveats: I3D 2014 paper, CGAL 4.2 is very old; compiler and flags not stated ('compiled with optimization enabled'); GPU (CUDA) vs sequential CPU CGAL, so the comparison is hardware-asymmetric; repo inactive since 2018.

notes: Paper PDF ships in the repo, so benchmark_url moved off the third-party codeyarns copy. BSD-3-Clause confirmed from README license text; 185 stars; last commit 2018-03-26 (abandoned).

tier_reason: Research paper (arXiv 1805.08831, by the Gmsh authors) times CGAL 4.12 against HXT on named CPUs; no compiler/flags stated, so not A. First-party authors, but a peer-reviewed-style paper; B kept.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Sequential: ~2 s for 1M points vs ~6 s for CGAL/TetGen/Geogram (about 3x, abstract); parallel on 64-core Xeon Phi 7210, 10M points: 4.48 s vs CGAL 4.12 20.15 s, CGAL did not complete 10^8 points (Fig. 11b); 3 billion tetrahedra in 53 s on AMD EPYC
corrections.caveats: Compiler and flags not stated in the paper; repo_url is the live-clones mirror of canonical gitlab.onelab.info/gmsh/gmsh; 2018 paper so CGAL 4.12 is old; authors are Gmsh developers (first-party); last_commit is for Gmsh as a whole; GPL-2.0-or-later with a linking exception.

notes: Numbers checked in the arXiv PDF (v3). I did not confirm the journal venue (believed published in IJNME, unverified), so tier B rests on it being a research paper; orchestrator may retier to C if strict on first-party. Mirror: 127 stars, last commit 2026-09-28.
